## Summary

What this change does and why. One or two sentences — the *why* matters more
than the *what*. If this fixes an issue, reference it here (e.g. `Closes #12`).

## Test plan

What you ran, and on what. `cargo xtask ci` runs everything CI does in one
command; `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
--all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` must be
clean before this is mergeable — a warning is a build failure in CI.

Say whether you ran it **on a real GPU / real Windows machine**. CI has
neither: the Linux job renders on Mesa's software rasteriser and the Windows
job only proves the build links. A visual or driver-dependent change needs a
screenshot, or bench numbers from a real machine. The CI run uploads the
rendered frames (the `bench-*` artifacts) so a reviewer can see what a
shader change did without checking the branch out.

## Checklist

- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes
- [ ] Windows cross-check: `cargo clippy … --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`
- [ ] No new `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` — not even in tests
- [ ] New files carry the module header banner (`Module:` / `Description:` /
      `Dependencies:`)
- [ ] Any new `unsafe` is a one-call safe leaf in `strobe-gfx/src/gl/` with a
      `// SAFETY:` comment
- [ ] Per-frame path changed → bench before/after recorded in `docs/BENCHMARKS.md`
- [ ] Visual or UI change → screenshot or contact sheet attached
- [ ] `docs/ROADMAP.md` updated; new decisions logged in `docs/DECISIONS.md`
- [ ] Commit messages use the `feat:` / `fix:` / `perf:` / `refactor:` /
      `docs:` / `test:` / `build:` / `ci:` prefixes (they build `CHANGELOG.md`)
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` not hand-edited — it is generated by `cargo xtask changelog`

Full guidelines, including how to build and what CI enforces, are in
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md).
